title: Equal Rational Numbers
description:
Given two strings `s` and `t` representing non-negative rational numbers, return whether they represent exactly the same number.

Each string has one of these forms: `IntegerPart`, `IntegerPart.NonRepeatingPart`, or `IntegerPart.NonRepeatingPart(RepeatingPart)`. Parentheses denote digits repeated forever. The non-repeating part may be empty, as in `1.` or `1.(9)`.

For example, `0.1(6)`, `0.1666(6)`, and `0.166(66)` all represent `1/6`. An infinite sequence of nines is interpreted exactly, so `0.(9)` equals `1`.

## Examples

### Example 1

```text
Input: s = "0.(52)", t = "0.5(25)"
Output: true
```

### Example 2

```text
Input: s = "0.1666(6)", t = "0.166(66)"
Output: true
```

### Example 3

```text
Input: s = "0.9(9)", t = "1."
Output: true
```

## Constraints

- Each part consists only of decimal digits.
- The integer part has no leading zeros except for zero itself.
- 1 <= IntegerPart.length <= 4
- 0 <= NonRepeatingPart.length <= 4
- 1 <= RepeatingPart.length <= 4 when present.
- Each string follows one of the three forms above.
